items.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025
items.q: Yeah no I love Satie, so I just decided to let my intuition write that.

ctx.x: Yes. It’s the piece, your tribute to Erik Satie. Your solo piano work.

Oh you mean from the Newvelle solo, yeah. Yeah no I love Satie, so I just decided to let my intuition write that. So instead of it being in 3/4 like “Gymnopedie” is, I wrote it in 4/4. But I did use some of the, shall we say the things that Satie used in “Gymnopedie.” And it’s like F sharp, which is like a half-step down from where “Gymnopedie” is, which is in G. And also the bridge went to E flat and then back to F sharp.

When you got to the end of that, writing it, or near the end, was there a debate in your mind about — because I noticed you ended it in the relative minor where the bridge had gone. And it leaves a different impression, at least for me, than if you had played like a lovely F sharp major 7 or something like that. Do you recall why you made that decision?
